title: Finance vs Operating Leases
description: Learn the major criteria used to classify leases and understand why classification matters.
html:
Lessee lease classification

Under U.S. GAAP, a lessee generally classifies a lease as either a finance lease or an operating lease.

Finance lease indicators

A lease is classified as a finance lease when it meets one or more of the applicable classification criteria.

  1. Ownership of the underlying asset transfers to the lessee by the end of the lease.
  2. The lessee has a purchase option that is reasonably certain to be exercised.
  3. The lease term is for a major part of the remaining economic life of the asset.
  4. The present value of lease payments plus certain residual value guarantees equals or exceeds substantially all of the asset's fair value.
  5. The asset is so specialized that it is expected to have no alternative use to the lessor at the end of the lease term.

If none of those criteria are met

The lessee generally classifies the lease as an operating lease.

Finance Lease

Meets at least one applicable finance lease classification criterion.

Operating Lease

Does not meet the finance lease classification criteria.

Don't memorize fake bright-line rules

You may encounter old study material referring mechanically to rules such as 75% of economic life or 90% of fair value.

Current U.S. GAAP uses principles such as major part and substantially all.

CPA habit

Look at the facts of the lease and evaluate the classification criteria rather than blindly applying an outdated numerical rule.

quiz.prompt: A lease transfers ownership of the underlying asset to the lessee at the end of the lease term. From the lessee's perspective, this is an indicator of:
quiz.explanation: Transfer of ownership by the end of the lease term is one of the finance lease classification criteria.
